question.:question/problem:
The temperature $T(t),$ in degrees Celsius, of a cooling iron can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.16(T-29)
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, measured in minutes. If the initial temperature of the iron is ${166}^{∘}C,$ calculate its temperature after $5$ minutes. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We're told that the temperature of the cooling iron is modeled by the inhibited decay equation

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.16(T-29).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{T-29} & =-0.16\,dt \\ \int \frac{dT}{T-29} & =-\int 0.16\,\text{d}t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|T-29| & =-0.16t+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited decay equation, we have $T-29>0$ for all $t>0.$
Next, we solve for $T(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T-29 & ={e}^{-0.16t+C} \\ T-29 & ={e}^{C}{e}^{-0.16t} \\ T-29 & =K{e}^{-0.16t} \\ T & =29+K{e}^{-0.16t}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration. 

We're told that the initial temperature of the iron was ${166}^{∘}C.$ So, we apply the initial condition $T(0)=166,$ and solve for $K:$

$$
\begin{aligned}166 & =29+K{e}^{0} \\ 166 & =29+K \\ K & =137\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is

$$
T(t)=29+137{e}^{-0.16t}.
$$

Finally, the temperature of the iron after $t=5$ minutes is

$$
T(5)=29+137{e}^{-0.16\cdot 5}≈{91}^{∘}\text{C},
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

generation.domain: T(t)>ambient; positive rate; t>=0; observations strictly cooling
